bullets.text: Adam Duguid (Project Manager), Ebenezer Ademesoye (Marketing Expert), Tarik Rahman (Industrial Designer), and Dave Cochrane (User Interface Designer) introduced themselves.
The meeting agenda includes opening, acquaintance, tool training, project plan discussion, and closing.
The goal is to design a new remote control that is original, trendy, and user-friendly to stand out from existing products.

The project will proceed through three phases: functional (user requirement spec, technical functions, working design), architectural (conceptual components, properties, materials), and detailed design (analysis of design so far).
The team drew animals on a whiteboard to start the acquaintance phase: Ebenezer drew an elephant, Tarik drew a tiger, and Dave drew a monkey.

Ebenezer explained elephants have good memories and are big, strong, and gentle. Tarik explained tigers are the biggest cats and he loves their stripes. Dave explained he chose a monkey because his daughter is affectionately known as Miss Monkey and monkeys have attitude.
Target price is 12.5 Euros per unit with a retail price of 25 Euros to aim for 50 million Euros in sales.
High-end market exists for touch screen LCD remotes with sophisticated programming, macros, and integration, but this is prohibitive for the current price range.
Proposed a remote that combines conventional push buttons with macro capabilities to control multiple units in an integrated fashion.
Ideas include a single button to turn on multiple devices (TV, recorder, sound system) or a play button that turns on the TV and selects the channel.
Consideration of gaming remotes with large buttons for interactive television and angle changes, including a bar-code design for recording.
Discussion of using a control pad (stick-on) instead of buttons for gaming and navigation, similar to console interfaces.
The remote should be ergonomic, biomorphic in shape to fit the hand comfortably, yet small, stylish, and slightly unconventional.
Key features include a macro facility requiring programming and significant response back, and an interface familiar to users (control pad/keypad).
